chunks: And Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn 'Uqda al-Kufi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qoob narrated to me, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from his father, from Ya'qoob ibn Shu'ayb, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah saying:
No, by Allah! Allah does not leave this matter aside unless He specifies ones, who will undertake it until the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.يَقُومُ بِهِ: To undertake/stand for it (to uphold and execute the authority)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say about the continuity of divine authority until the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the doctrine of *al-amr* (divine authority/command) as an unbroken chain of Imams, ensuring that God never leaves the earth without a *Hujjah* (proof) to guide humanity. This affirmation underscores the Shia belief in the necessity (*wujub*) of the Imamate for the preservation of divine law and spiritual guidance until the Day of Resurrection. The statement highlights the continuity of prophetic legacy through the Ahl al-Bayt, serving as a foundational text for the concept of the Hidden Imam.
